Weddings

What We Plan

Every Tradition Honored. Every Detail Considered.

Every wedding is a beautiful combination of traditions, family, and unforgettable moments. From mehndi, haldi, and sangeet to the ceremony and reception, we ensure every celebration receives the attention it deserves.

Anvaya brings together venues, trusted vendors, budgets, and family needs through one thoughtful plan. Our strong vendor relationships help us secure competitive pricing without compromising on quality or service, while we coordinate every detail so you can enjoy your celebration.

We plan Indian, Pakistani, Bangladeshi, Sikh, South Indian, Muslim, Hindu, Christian, and interfaith weddings across South Florida, honoring the traditions that make your celebration uniquely yours.

Questions Couples Ask

Frequently Asked Wedding Planning Questions

When should we hire an Indian wedding planner in South Florida?

For a multi-event wedding, starting 12–18 months ahead often allows more venue and vendor choices, especially during popular dates. A shorter timeline can still work depending on availability, guest count and flexibility.

Does Anvaya plan Pakistani, Sikh and other South Asian weddings?

Yes. Our planning approach accommodates Indian, Pakistani, Bangladeshi, Sikh, Hindu, Muslim, Christian and multicultural celebrations. We learn your exact customs with your family and officiants rather than assuming every wedding follows the same traditions.

Can we use vendors we have already selected?

Absolutely. We can coordinate with your existing venue, caterer, décor team or other suppliers, review the remaining needs and bring everyone into a connected schedule.

What affects the cost of wedding planning?

The scope depends on the number of events, guest count, venues, travel requirements, design and production complexity, and how much planning support you need. We discuss the scope and fee before you commit.

Can you coordinate a wedding across multiple venues and days?

Yes. We can connect event schedules, vendor arrivals, ceremony timing, guest transportation and venue transitions across a multi-day wedding weekend. The result is one coordinated plan rather than separate events competing for attention.
